kf: **SJS/TEN** are severe drug reactions with widespread keratinocyte death: **SJS <10%**, overlap 10–30%, **TEN >30%** body surface detachment.
Prodrome of fever and sore eyes/throat, then painful dusky macules, atypical flat targets, blisters, **Nikolsky sign** and **≥2 mucosal sites**.
Culprits started **4–28 days** earlier: allopurinol, aromatic anticonvulsants, lamotrigine, sulfonamides (co-trimoxazole), nevirapine, oxicam NSAIDs.
Stop all non-essential drugs; **999 / same-day** transfer to a burns or dermatology intensive unit; ophthalmology within 24 h.
SCORTEN predicts mortality (about 10% in SJS, 30%+ in TEN); record the allergy and Yellow Card.

sub: Rare (1–6 per million per year); higher risk with HIV, lupus, cancer and HLA-B*15:02 (carbamazepine in South-East Asian people).

myths: **"Blisters on lips and eyes are just cold sores"**: mucositis with a new drug and skin pain is SJS until proven otherwise.
patho_lead: Drug-specific **cytotoxic T cells** trigger mass **keratinocyte apoptosis**, so the whole epidermis peels away.

mech.t: The drug binds specific HLA molecules and activates CD8+ T cells and NK cells.
Granulysin, perforin/granzyme and Fas–FasL kill keratinocytes.
The entire epidermis dies and separates from the dermis.
mech.cap: Normal skin (left) versus toxic epidermal necrolysis (right): full-thickness epidermal necrosis detaching as a sheet with sparse dermal inflammation.

mech.t: Eyes, mouth, genitals and airway are affected the same way, causing scarring.

histo: Full-thickness epidermal necrosis with sparse dermal inflammation; frozen section can distinguish from SSSS (split high in epidermis).

sub: Mycoplasma causes mucositis-predominant disease (MIRM); also consider SSSS (painful red skin, superficial peeling, mucosa spared).

comp: Sepsis, fluid loss, respiratory failure; eye scarring and blindness, strictures, nail and hair loss, pigmentation; death.
prog: Mortality depends on SCORTEN; survivors often have long-term eye and skin problems.
